member.summary: Column-oriented store for one model parameter's wide-format output file: one row per element, one column for the element index, one per element identifier, and one per calendar year.

remarks.para: This replaces the one-Dictionary<string, object>-per-row shape that CSVHelper produces. That shape stores the column name again for every row and holds every value as a string, which measured at 68 bytes to hold an 8-byte number. Here a numeric column is a double[] and a text column is an int[] of codes over a pooled string[], so the same data costs 8 and ~4 bytes per cell respectively.
A table is immutable once built. Build one from a file with JCass_PostProcessing.Utilities.ParameterCsvReader, or in memory with .

member.name: T:JCass_PostProcessing.Utilities.ParameterCsvReader
member.summary: Reads wide-format parameter output files straight into columns.

remarks.para: Nothing here builds a jcDataSet on the way. Reading into rows first and converting afterwards would lower resident memory but leave peak memory and load time exactly where they are, which is half of what the column store exists to fix. Fields go into the typed arrays directly.

There are two read paths and they must agree. A file is read by splitting lines on commas, which read the production snapshot roughly three times faster than tokenising it did. The moment a " appears anywhere in a line, that pass is abandoned and the whole file is re-read with - never just the offending line, because a quoted field may contain a newline and a line is then no longer a row. The fast path therefore has to reproduce two behaviours of that are easy to miss: it skips blank lines, and it trims white space from every field.

Every parse pins . The reader this replaces went through Convert.ToDouble(string) at the point of use, which follows the current culture - a latent bug on a host whose locale uses a comma decimal separator.

A cell that will not parse becomes NaN, and never stops the load. A blank cell is a missing value and is silently NaN. A non-blank cell that will not parse is also NaN, but warns once per column, naming the file, the column and the first offending row. Throwing here would take down the whole config tag - the parameter set is loaded inside OutputSet.LoadData alongside treatments, spending and raw input - and so would break operations that never read parameter data at all.

member.summary: Reads every parameter file of a run, holding one copy of the identifier columns for the whole set instead of one copy per file.
member.param: The files to read, in the order the parameters are declared.
The element index and identifier columns, with the kind each is stored as. These are written from one source in one pass by the exporter, so they are identical in every file.
Called with a message for each recoverable problem. Defaults to when not supplied.
member.returns: One table per parameter, keyed by parameter name.
member.remarks:
Identifier columns are parsed from every file and compared against the first file's, then discarded. The comparison costs nothing - the parser hands over the text either way and the duplicate dies in gen 0 - and it buys full verification for no storage.
A file whose identifiers differ keeps its own, and only warns. It cannot arise from a normal export, but an interrupted or partial re-export can produce it, and such a folder loads and answers every question correctly today - no consumer cross-references identifiers between parameter files. Throwing would take the client's whole config tag offline to save a few megabytes.
